questions.question: For y = 6/x, the asymptotes are:
The domain of y = 6/x is:
options: All real x except x = 0, because division by zero is undefined

questions.question: A hyperbola of the form y = a/x + q has:
options: NO y-intercept, because x = 0 is excluded from the domain

subtopics.title: The Exponential Graph — Growth, Decay and Its Asymptote

questions.question: For y = 2ˣ, the value at x = −3 is:
The range of y = 2ˣ is:
options: y > 0 strictly, because 2 to any power is positive but never zero

questions.question: Every graph of the form y = bˣ passes through:
options: (0; 1), because b to the power 0 is 1 for every base

questions.question: Why may the base b not equal 1?
options: Because 1 is not a whole number
Because the graph would be undefined
Because the range would be negative
Because 1 to any power is 1, giving a horizontal line rather than an exponential curve

questions.question: For y = 2ˣ − 4, the asymptote and y-intercept are:
The x-intercept of y = 2ˣ − 4 is:
For y = −2ˣ + 8, the range is:
options: y < 8, because subtracting a positive quantity from 8 always leaves less than 8

questions.question: Which is an exhibit from the error museum?
options: Drawing the asymptote as a dashed line
Writing the range of y = 2ˣ as y > 0
Drawing a curve that touches or crosses its own asymptote

questions.question: A fixed R120 fare split between 4 passengers costs each:
The two impossibilities in the shared-fare story become which two features of the graph?
options: Two asymptotes — the share never reaches zero, and you cannot share among nobody

questions.question: Going from 2 to 3 passengers saves each person R20, but going from 11 to 12 saves less than a rand. On the graph this shows as:
options: A curve that drops steeply at first and then flattens out

questions.question: Why does the shared-fare curve never cross the up-and-down axis?
options: Because the numbers get too large
Because the curve has two branches
Because you can never put zero in — there is no such thing as sharing among zero people

questions.question: One teller, then two, then four, then eight — this is growth by:
Running the doubling backwards gives a half, a quarter, an eighth… The point is that:
options: You can halve forever and always have something left, so the curve never lands on the bottom line

questions.question: Every one of these curves passes through the same free point, because:
options: Anything to the power zero is one, so the crossing on the up-and-down axis is at 1

questions.question: A cellphone battery losing half its remaining charge each hour gives a curve that:
options: Crosses the bottom line and continues
Starts high on the left and slides down toward the bottom line, never touching it

questions.question: The sketching routine begins with:
options: Drawing the dashed line the curve will not touch

questions.question: For a graph shifted down four, writing 'asymptote at zero' is wrong because:
options: The line the curve avoids moves with the graph — here it is four units below zero
Zero is not a valid answer

questions.question: Solving 2ˣ − 4 = 0 for the crossing of the flat axis gives:
The 'ground floor or upstairs?' question separates:
options: y = x², which turns around, from y = 2ˣ, which never turns
